stem: A business wants to accumulate a sinking fund of Rs 46,410 by making equal annual deposits at the end of each year for 4 years. The deposits earn 10% per annum compounded annually. What annual deposit is required?  [Given: (1.1)^4 = 1.4641]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Dividing the target Rs 46,410 by 4 (the number of periods) without accounting for compounding gives Rs 11,602.50, a simple division with no discounting.

Dividing by the annuity-due factor [4.641 x 1.1 = 5.1051] instead of the ordinary annuity factor gives Rs 46,410 / 5.1051 = Rs 9,090.91; this applies end-of-year formula logic to a beginning-of-year formula.
Using n = 5 instead of n = 4: FV factor = [(1.1)^5-1]/0.1 = (1.6105-1)/0.1 = 6.105; A = 46410/6.105 = Rs 7,602, an off-by-one period error.

explanation_sections.punchline: Divide the required FV by the FV annuity factor to find the equal periodic deposit - it is the FV formula solved in reverse.
explanation_sections.lesson: Whenever a target future amount is given and the payment is unknown, invert the FV annuity formula: A = FV x i / [(1+i)^n - 1].
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds. Compute the factor, then divide. Trap: option 1 = simple division; option 4 uses wrong n.
